tasks.short: Gather and organize evidence about operational problems and procedures.

steps.what: Define the problem, study boundaries and evidence needed.
Retrieve operational records and export relevant transactions.
Interview process participants about actual practices, exceptions and missing records.
Read procedures and notes, then organize source-linked observations.

loop.input: Approved procedure documents and analyst-written interview notes.
loop.output: Observations with source locations, dates and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Require valid source locations and supporting quotations; analyst checks interpretation and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unresolved items enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Descriptions and informal practices vary too much for fixed field extraction.

steps.what: Resolve conflicting observations and identify evidence gaps.

tasks.design: Configure an evidence register in the {WORKFLOW}, with source links into the {DOCS}; scheduled readers collect approved extracts from the {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}. A bounded extraction loop proposes observations from documents and notes, while the analyst resolves contradictions and conducts interviews.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources have different identifiers, access rules and formats. Interviews expose undocumented practices that exports cannot reveal.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors and validation rules. Bounded extraction can organize varied text without deciding which account is true.
tasks.still_hard: Obtaining access, establishing source reliability and learning why people bypass procedures remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Ask sensitive follow-up questions and distinguish missing evidence from a misleading problem statement.

ambition.what: A short diagnostic service for small departmental improvement requests.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time collecting files and more time testing the problem definition with process participants. No new approval rights follow automatically.

reach.task: Trace operational fields to their source records.
reach.learn: Data lineage, stable identifiers and access boundaries.

evidence.claim: Structured records can be collected and organized with deterministic integrations and a records app.
Free-text extraction needs source checks and analyst review; the proposed time reductions are estimates.
In the Netherlands, works council consent can apply to employee-data and monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: This is a representative study of a cross-functional operational process, not a measured customer workflow.
Approved exports can be used where direct interfaces are unavailable.
The study examines processes rather than scoring individual workers.
Build ranges describe a first usable scope and exclude waiting time for formal consultation.
unknowns: Which operational sources and export permissions are available?
Which procedure documents are current and authoritative?
Does the planned collection involve employee monitoring or consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: How reliably does extraction preserve contradictory accounts and source locations?
What access-minimization pattern works across the selected source categories?
new_work: Review extracted observations and repair source links.
Handle failed exports and changed source fields.
Maintain evidence categories, retention rules and access permissions.
tasks.statement: Gather and organize information on problems or procedures.

tasks.short: Analyze evidence and develop practical alternatives for improving operations.

steps.what: Clean, join and reconcile study extracts.
Calculate baseline costs, delays, volumes and process variation.
Develop causal hypotheses and alternative ways to operate.
Model alternative costs, capacity requirements, benefits and sensitivity to assumptions.
Challenge assumptions with process owners and select options for recommendation.

tasks.design: A versioned job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} validates extracts and supplies baseline measures to the {BI}. A deterministic scenario generator calculates alternatives from explicit assumptions and exports tables to the {DOCS}. The analyst develops causal explanations and tests practical trade-offs with process owners.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each study needs data reconciliation, agreed metric definitions and a model of the specific process.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes repeatable validation and scenario tools cheaper to build. Standard calculations can be reused without delegating causal reasoning to a model.
tasks.still_hard: Observational data rarely proves causation. Unrecorded constraints, uncertain demand and disputed cost allocation can dominate the answer.
tasks.human_edge: Identify plausible causes, design useful tests and recognize alternatives that look efficient but fail operationally.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of the next bottleneck experiment during an improvement pilot.

tasks.altitude: The analyst reruns calculations quickly and spends more time designing experiments and challenging assumptions. They can propose pilot priorities; spending authority still depends on delegation.

reach.task: Test queue, capacity and service-level trade-offs.
reach.learn: Flow variability, bottleneck analysis and sensitivity modelling.

reach.task: Distinguish stable process variation from meaningful deterioration.
reach.learn: Control limits, sampling and evidence for process changes.

evidence.claim: Data validation, baseline calculations and scenario arithmetic are suitable for deterministic implementation.
A scenario calculator does not establish causation or prove organizational feasibility.
Operational optimization software is an adjacent capability, not evidence for automating management judgement.

assumptions: The analysis concerns a measurable operating process with usable volume, timing and cost data.
Metric definitions and scenario assumptions are supplied or agreed by people.
Unresolved data exceptions block affected calculations rather than being silently imputed.
The design excludes individual worker evaluation and automated employment decisions.
Build ranges cover one process model and reuse the evidence collection foundation where available.
unknowns: Are timestamps, identifiers and cost allocations reliable enough for the proposed measures?
Who can agree metric definitions and scenario assumptions?
Can the team run a pilot that tests the proposed causal explanation?
Which data uses require consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Which process model is accurate enough for the decisions without unnecessary complexity?
Which sensitivity checks expose recommendations that depend on fragile assumptions?
new_work: Investigate data exceptions and baseline discrepancies.
Validate formulas against independent worked examples.
Maintain scenario assumptions and model versions.
Compare pilot outcomes with predicted benefits.
tasks.statement: Analyze data gathered and develop solutions or alternative methods of proceeding.

tasks.short: Work with employees and managers to make new systems and procedures function successfully.

steps.what: Review rollout progress, operating measures and reported issues.
Arrange check-ins and circulate the discussion brief.
Discuss practical difficulties, clarify expectations and agree possible remedies.
Authorize procedure adjustments, resources or rollback within delegated limits.
Write the action record and assign agreed follow-up work.

loop.input: Analyst-written discussion notes and approved remedies.
loop.output: Draft action record with owners, dates and approval references.
loop.check: Analyst confirms every commitment; missing owners or dates remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per meeting; analyst finishes ambiguous records.
loop.why_not_simpler: Informal notes require interpretation to distinguish suggestions from agreed commitments.

steps.what: Check whether agreed actions solved the operational problem.

tasks.design: Configure check-in scheduling and action reminders through the {WORKFLOW}, {CALENDAR} and {PROJECT}, with a factual brief assembled from the {HELPDESK} and {BI}. A bounded loop drafts action records from analyst notes, with approval before assignments are written. Conversations and authorization of operational changes stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination combines scattered status information with trust, competing priorities and informal commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and reminder features can handle routine coordination. Small integrations and bounded drafting reduce preparation and paperwork.
tasks.still_hard: People may disagree about workload, success criteria or whether a workaround is acceptable.
tasks.human_edge: Make it safe to report failures, negotiate workable commitments and judge whether adoption is real.

ambition.what: Weekly rollout support-priority decisions during the first month after implementation.

tasks.altitude: More of the analyst's week goes to resolving adoption problems and verifying remedies. Operations managers retain change and resource authority.

reach.task: Manage rollout dependencies and follow-up actions.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping, escalation thresholds and benefits tracking.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, reminders and structured status briefs can use existing configuration and deterministic rules.
Adoption conversations and disputed commitments still require human participation.
Workplace emotion recognition is prohibited; it is excluded from this design.

assumptions: The task includes supporting preparation and follow-up, as well as the central conversation.
Participants are internal and the analyst may arrange routine check-ins.
The design uses written notes and aggregate operating measures, without call recording or worker scoring.
Build ranges assume existing project and calendar access; formal consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Who may authorize procedure changes and rollback?
Are action owners and due dates recorded consistently?
Would the proposed data use trigger consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Can note-to-action drafting reliably distinguish proposals, approvals and unresolved disagreements?
Which operating measures detect adoption problems without measuring individual employees?
new_work: Review action drafts before assignments are written.
Resolve unassigned actions and misleading status signals.
Maintain reminder timing, escalation rules and participant lists.
tasks.statement: Confer with personnel concerned to ensure successful functioning of newly implemented systems or procedures.

tasks.short: Design, introduce and check a programme for storing, protecting, retrieving and retaining business records.

steps.what: Inventory record types, repositories, owners and existing access controls.
Agree record classes, retention needs, access responsibilities and retrieval requirements.
Draft the filing scheme, retention schedule and records handling procedures.

loop.input: Agreed records requirements, existing policy and approved procedure template.
loop.output: Draft procedures with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check every retention rule against approved requirements; reject invented periods and unsupported legal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per section; unresolved conflicts return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but local handling instructions require rewriting source prose.

steps.what: Approve retention rules, access responsibilities and the programme rollout.
Configure filing locations, metadata, permissions and retention controls.
Explain new filing responsibilities and practise retrieval with departmental representatives.
Sample records and check filing, access, retention and retrieval compliance.
Authorize corrections and resolve disputed retention, access or disposal exceptions.

tasks.design: Configure classification, access and retention controls in the {DOCS}, with a records register in the {WORKFLOW} where existing metadata is insufficient. Read-only connectors on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assemble inventory and compliance evidence; a bounded drafting loop prepares procedures from agreed requirements. The records owner approves policy, control deployment and disputed disposal actions, while a {BI} dashboard shows exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repository metadata and ownership were inconsistent. Software could enforce rules, but people still had to settle retention duties and cross-department responsibilities.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing repository controls cover much of the execution. AI-assisted coding makes small connectors and checks cheaper to build; bounded drafting reduces procedure preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy migrations, legal holds, poor metadata and conflicting retention duties remain costly. GDPR applies; employee consultation and works-council requirements depend on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve competing business, privacy and evidential needs, and secure agreement on who is accountable for records.

ambition.what: Records readiness review for new internal projects

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling inventories and more time resolving ownership gaps and testing retrieval. Within an agreed remit, they can require records requirements before a project launches; retention and disposal authority stays with the records owner.

reach.task: Resolve misfiled records and missing metadata.
reach.learn: Learn practical classification problems and how staff search for records.

reach.task: Set departmental records responsibilities during organisational changes.
reach.learn: Learn service ownership, escalation paths and rollout planning.

evidence.claim: Repository configuration can enforce metadata, access and retention rules once those rules are agreed.
Cross-repository inventory and compliance checks usually need connectors, mappings and human exception review.
GDPR applies to personal records; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed controls.

assumptions: The first release covers selected repositories and record classes, rather than a complete historical migration.
A records owner can obtain legal advice and approve retention requirements.
Repository metadata can be read through supported interfaces or controlled exports.
Inventory checks use metadata where possible, limiting access to record contents.
unknowns: Which repositories, retention features and export interfaces are available?
Who can approve access changes, legal holds and disposal?
How complete are record ownership and classification metadata?
Which national rules, employee consultation duties and collective agreements apply?
Does the proposed processing require a GDPR impact assessment?
research_questions: Which record classes generate the most retrieval failures or retention disputes?
Can existing repository features replace a separate records register?
What evidence is needed to demonstrate that a record was retained, held or disposed of correctly?
new_work: Review inventory gaps and compliance exceptions.
Maintain repository connectors and record-class mappings.
Check drafted procedures against approved requirements.
Test retrieval and access controls after organisational changes.
Review proposed disposal actions and maintain legal holds.
tasks.statement: Develop and implement records management program for filing, protection, and retrieval of records, and assure compliance with program.

tasks.short: Review forms and reports with managers and users, then agree improvements to purpose, format and distribution.

steps.what: Collect current forms, report samples and distribution lists
Inspect source fields, report runs and available usage records
Compare fields, frequency and recipients to flag duplication and gaps
Discuss purpose, usability, missing information and distribution with managers and users
Draft recommendations and revised form or report specifications

loop.input: User requirements, review findings, comparison results and relevant policy.
loop.output: Change proposal and specification with each change linked to a requirement or finding.
loop.check: Validate required fields and change traceability. Analyst checks meaning, access implications and unresolved conflicts.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per proposal. Conflicting requirements stay flagged for decision.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text requirements need contextual synthesis; fixed templates cannot explain trade-offs or reconcile terminology.

steps.what: Approve which forms and reports to change, retain or retire
Copy approved actions into a separate tracking workbook

tasks.design: An inventory service links forms in the {DOCS} to report metadata from the {ERP} and {BI}, then applies deterministic checks for repeated fields, stale schedules and recipient differences. A bounded loop drafts specifications from confirmed user requirements, while the process owner records change or retirement decisions in the {WORKFLOW}. Those approved records become delivery items in the {PROJECT}, removing the separate {SPREADSHEET} tracker.
tasks.previous_blocker: No single inventory connected document versions, report definitions and recipients. Usage evidence rarely explained why a form or report mattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata connectors and deterministic comparisons make the inventory maintainable. Bounded drafting reduces the effort of turning discussions into traceable specifications.
tasks.still_hard: Low usage does not prove low value. Rarely used reports may support controls, legal duties or emergency decisions, and users may disagree on essential fields.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst establishes what decision each report supports and negotiates between user needs, controls and administrative burden.

ambition.what: A quarterly decision on retiring redundant management reports.

tasks.altitude: The analyst shifts from collecting examples to facilitating decisions about information needs. With an agreed mandate, they can prioritise the review queue; report retirement still requires owner approval.

reach.task: Translate approved report changes into field, validation and access requirements.
reach.learn: Data lineage, schema constraints and acceptance criteria.

reach.task: Identify superseded forms while preserving required records.
reach.learn: Retention schedules, version control and record classification.

evidence.claim: Metadata inventories and deterministic comparisons can identify candidate duplication without deciding business necessity.
A single approved action record can feed delivery tracking and remove duplicate workbook maintenance.
Usage records involving identifiable employees require a GDPR assessment; national consultation requirements depend on the use.

assumptions: Some report metadata and usage records are available; missing usage remains unknown rather than zero.
Initial comparisons use explicit field mappings and exact rules; semantic matching is not assumed.
Validated findings are reused when a broader organisational study exists.
Approval records can become the authoritative change tracker.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Usage analysis concerns report utility, not individual worker evaluation.
unknowns: Which report definitions, distribution lists and usage records can be retrieved?
Who owns each form, report and retention decision?
Which apparently redundant reports serve legal, audit or contingency needs?
Can the approval record replace the separate tracking workbook?
Does usage collection introduce employee monitoring under national rules?
research_questions: How often do deterministic duplication flags identify a genuinely removable report?
Does low report usage predict low decision value?
Can users complete representative work with the revised form or specification?
new_work: Resolve ownership and metadata gaps.
Maintain field mappings and comparison rules.
Verify generated specifications against user requirements.
Investigate low-usage reports before proposing retirement.
Check that approved changes reach delivery and obsolete versions are withdrawn.
tasks.statement: Review forms and reports and confer with management and users about format, distribution, and purpose, identifying problems and improvements.

tasks.short: Interview staff and observe work to understand actual processes and resource use.

steps.what: Prepare interview questions and an observation checklist

loop.input: Approved study plan, existing procedures and a question library.
loop.output: Interview guide and observation checklist linked to study questions.
loop.check: Analyst checks coverage, neutral wording and whether questions fit the work setting.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass. Analyst writes unresolved or sensitive questions manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed question library cannot fully adapt to undocumented procedures and situational study questions.

steps.what: Arrange interviews and observation visits around staff availability
Interview staff about work, exceptions, handoffs and practical constraints
Observe work on site and record methods, equipment, delays and workarounds
Consolidate notes into process findings and unresolved questions

loop.input: Analyst-written interview notes and observation logs, with study questions.
loop.output: Findings draft separating observed facts, reported claims and analyst interpretations.
loop.check: Require source references for findings. Analyst checks omissions, contradictions and inappropriate attribution.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per evidence batch. Ambiguous notes remain open questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes describe similar activities differently and require contextual grouping.

steps.what: Confirm factual descriptions and record disputed interpretations

tasks.design: A study workspace in the {WORKFLOW} prepares guides from approved material in the {DOCS} and coordinates visits through the {CALENDAR}. Interviews and observation remain human; a bounded loop converts analyst-written notes into traceable findings for participant validation. Access controls in the {DOCS} restrict identifiable notes separately from wider study findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observation depends on physical context and trust. Notes varied in structure, making synthesis slow and difficult to trace.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable forms and scheduling configuration reduce coordination. Bounded extraction can organise notes while preserving links to the analyst's evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Staff may describe the official process rather than actual practice. Observation can change behaviour, and disagreement cannot be settled by summarising notes.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst notices workarounds, asks tactful follow-up questions and earns candid explanations.

ambition.what: Include rotating-shift staff in process discovery through shorter, prepared visits.

tasks.altitude: Most of the week still involves interviews and observation. Less preparation and note assembly creates room for follow-up visits; formal decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Observe a process and distinguish procedural gaps from justified local adaptations.
reach.learn: Evidence sampling, nonconformity definitions and corrective-action interviews.

reach.task: Investigate how workplace layout contributes to delays.
reach.learn: Site access, physical constraints and safe observation practices.

evidence.claim: Scheduling configuration and structured observation forms can reduce administration without replacing fieldwork.
Bounded extraction can organise free-text notes, but factual interpretation still needs human checking.
The EU AI Act prohibits workplace emotion recognition, subject to its stated exceptions.

assumptions: The workflow uses analyst-written notes; it does not require audio, video or automated emotion inference.
The time split keeps most effort in direct conversation and observation, consistent with the supplied priors.
Participant validation confirms factual descriptions; it does not give participants a veto over independent conclusions.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR governs identifiable notes. Access, retention and employee consultation follow applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which shifts, locations and roles need representation?
Can participants speak confidentially without their line manager present?
What note retention, attribution and employee consultation requirements apply?
Who can authorise safe access to operational sites?
research_questions: Do shorter prepared visits capture the same exceptions as longer unstructured interviews?
Does extraction preserve minority accounts and contradictions?
Does participant validation reveal systematic gaps in observation?
new_work: Check extracted findings against original notes.
Resolve contradictions through further interviews or observation.
Maintain question libraries and observation checklists.
Apply note access, retention and deletion rules.
tasks.statement: Interview personnel and conduct on-site observation to ascertain unit functions, work performed, and methods, equipment, and personnel used.

tasks.short: Document study findings and recommend operational or organizational changes.

steps.what: Collect approved findings, option comparisons and supporting sources.
Draft findings, recommendations, implementation stages and limitations.

loop.input: Approved findings, selected options, scenario tables, pilot criteria and report template.
loop.output: Draft report with source-linked claims, limitations and an implementation outline.
loop.check: Insert numeric tables directly; require source links for factual claims and label unsupported proposals.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per report section; unresolved claims return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining findings and trade-offs requires prose tailored to the study and audience.

steps.what: Verify factual claims, figures, causal language and recommendation support.
Present recommendations, challenge feasibility and agree revisions with process owners.
Approve, defer or reject the proposed implementation scope and resource commitment.
File the final report and record the implementation handoff.

tasks.design: Keep approved findings and source links in the {DOCS}, so report preparation uses the existing evidence bundle without recollection. A template generator inserts verified tables and a bounded loop drafts the explanation; deterministic checks flag broken references and inconsistent figures for analyst review. The {WORKFLOW} records the sponsor's implementation decision before creating the authorized handoff in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report evidence is often scattered, while recommendations require both source accuracy and an audience-specific explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured evidence and versioned templates support deterministic assembly. Bounded drafting can turn approved material into reviewable prose.
tasks.still_hard: A cited source can still be misinterpreted. Organizational changes require careful treatment of uncertainty, employee impacts and disputed assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Make a defensible recommendation, explain uncomfortable findings and accept responsibility for its practical consequences.

ambition.what: A pilot decision pack that pairs each recommendation with a measurable test and stopping criteria.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling reports and more time shaping testable recommendations and discussing implementation. The sponsor retains resource and organizational-change decisions.

reach.task: Translate an approved recommendation into an implementation plan.
reach.learn: Dependencies, accountable owners, acceptance criteria and benefit measures.

reach.task: Assess disruption and recovery needs before a procedure change.
reach.learn: Impact analysis, fallback procedures and rollback conditions.

evidence.claim: Templates and deterministic table insertion can reduce report assembly work.
A documented report failure involving fabricated sources supports explicit source verification.
The proposed drafting workflow and remaining-time estimates are design estimates, not demonstrated case results.
Solely automated decisions with significant effects require assessment under GDPR Article 22.

assumptions: Report drafting starts after findings and option analysis are available.
The shared evidence bundle removes a separate collection step.
Analyst review includes final prose revisions before filing; the publication flow does not invent substantive changes.
A rollout plan is created only for approved implementation scope.
Build ranges cover report production and decision handoff, not implementation of the recommended changes.
EU law applies; employment and consultation requirements depend on applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which report format and approval delegation apply?
Which recommendations affect employee roles, monitoring or employment conditions?
Who must review employee impacts and any required consultation?
Can approved report versions and implementation decisions be linked in the existing systems?
research_questions: Which claim checks catch unsupported conclusions as well as missing citations?
How can version controls prevent approved figures from changing during report revision?
new_work: Review generated prose and verify that cited sources support each claim.
Maintain report templates, source-link checks and numeric consistency rules.
Resolve conflicting revisions and preserve the decision history.
Check that implementation handoffs match the sponsor's authorized scope.
tasks.statement: Document findings of study and prepare recommendations for implementation of new systems, procedures, or organizational changes.

tasks.short: Write operating manuals and train staff to use changed procedures, forms and equipment.

steps.what: Gather approved changes, current policies and equipment instructions
Draft the manual with steps, forms, examples and exception routes

loop.input: Approved procedure sources, equipment instructions and a manual template.
loop.output: Manual draft with source-linked instructions and flagged source conflicts.
loop.check: Validate document structure and references. Analyst walks through steps and checks exceptions against sources.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section. Conflicting or unsupported instructions go to the process owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot translate varied source documents into clear, role-specific instructions.

steps.what: Approve procedural accuracy, responsibilities and policy alignment
Publish the approved manual and replace the superseded version
Prepare role-specific exercises, quick guides and understanding checks

loop.input: Approved manual, role profiles and training templates.
loop.output: Role-specific exercises, quick guides and proposed answer keys.
loop.check: Analyst tests exercises against the manual. Training lead approves accuracy and audience suitability before use.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per role. Unclear answers or unsafe exercises require manual revision.
loop.why_not_simpler: Layout is deterministic, but useful scenarios and explanations depend on the changed procedure and audience.

steps.what: Invite affected staff and arrange training sessions
Demonstrate the procedure, coach practice and address staff questions
Record attendance, completion and follow-up training needs

tasks.design: A controlled generator assembles approved material from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}, then uses bounded loops to draft manuals and training packs. Existing approval and versioning in the {DOCS} release the manual, while the {WORKFLOW} coordinates invitations through the {CALENDAR} and records trainer-confirmed outcomes in the {LMS}. Live coaching remains human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source documents and training materials drifted apart. Producing consistent role-specific instructions required repeated writing and formatting.
tasks.enabler_now: Document APIs, version controls and reusable generators reduce assembly work. Bounded drafting can adapt approved instructions into exercises without inventing a new procedure.
tasks.still_hard: A readable manual can still describe an impractical procedure. Equipment training may require physical demonstration and competence checks by a qualified person.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst sees where learners struggle, adjusts explanations and distinguishes a training gap from a flawed procedure.

ambition.what: A role-specific change clinic using staff questions and practical exercises after each major procedure release.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time formatting manuals and more time coaching difficult transitions. With delegation, they can choose training formats and targeted follow-up; process owners retain procedure approval.

reach.task: Plan adoption support for a changed office procedure.
reach.learn: Service standards, staff coverage and adoption measures.

reach.task: Maintain controlled procedures and verify training effectiveness.
reach.learn: Document control, competence evidence and corrective-action follow-up.

evidence.claim: Document versioning, publication approvals, enrolment and completion records can use existing software configuration.
Source-grounded drafting can assist manual preparation, but procedural accuracy requires walkthroughs and accountable approval.
A documented Deloitte report case illustrates that generated text can contain nonexistent sources.

assumptions: The typical baseline includes a document store and basic learning records; their exact capabilities need confirmation.
Training records use trainer-confirmed attendance and explicit completion rules, not inferred worker competence.
The split preserves substantial writing and live training time, consistent with the supplied priors.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to learner records. National rules may require consultation when training records become worker monitoring.
unknowns: Which document approval, versioning and learning features are already licensed?
Which procedures require safety, legal or specialist approval?
Do any qualifications require observed practical assessment?
Are translations, accessible formats or offline training materials required?
Which consultation requirements apply to learning records and assessment?
research_questions: Can a learner complete the procedure using only the generated manual?
Do role-specific exercises improve practical performance over a generic presentation?
Can source changes reliably identify which training materials need revision?
new_work: Walk through generated instructions and verify answer keys.
Maintain source-to-manual and manual-to-training links.
Resolve conflicting source documents.
Handle failed enrolments and incomplete training evidence.
Review recurring learner questions and revise the procedure or training.
tasks.statement: Prepare manuals and train workers in use of new forms, reports, procedures or equipment, according to organizational policy.

tasks.short: Evaluate business forms and reports, design revisions, test them with users and approve controlled changes.

steps.what: Collect current forms, reports, change requests and completed examples.
Clarify the business purpose, user difficulties and decisions the artefact must support.
Map fields and calculations to source data, recipients and downstream dependencies.
Choose necessary fields, definitions, calculations and proposed changes.
Create revised layouts, instructions, validation rules and sample outputs.

loop.input: Field specification, approved templates, source instructions and wording requirements.
loop.output: Proposed labels and instructions inserted into deterministically generated layouts.
loop.check: Validate schema, required fields and calculations deterministically; check prose against source instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per artefact; unsupported wording goes to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Layout and validation are deterministic; changed instructions sometimes require rewriting free text. Skip the loop when approved wording exists.

steps.what: Observe users completing realistic cases and review report interpretations.
Approve the revised artefact and its effective date.
Publish the approved version, retire old copies and notify affected users.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to collect change requests and retrieve approved versions from the {DOCS}; connectors read declared dependencies from the {ERP} and {BI}. A deterministic generator builds layouts and validation tests, with a small drafting loop only for changed instructions. User testing and process-owner approval precede versioned publication through the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Form purpose and field definitions were often implicit. Manual version control and uncertain downstream dependencies made even small changes slow.
tasks.enabler_now: Schema-driven generation, existing approval features and inexpensive connector development reduce preparation work. A bounded loop can rewrite instructions without deciding which data the business needs.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden spreadsheet dependencies, conflicting metric definitions and inaccessible legacy formats remain difficult. Staff must test whether users understand the result.
tasks.human_edge: Decide which information earns its place, notice misleading reports and resolve disagreements about business meaning.

ambition.what: Pre-release form and report checks for small internal teams

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing comprehension and challenging unnecessary data collection. They can clear low-impact template changes within a delegated remit; process owners retain approval of business definitions and material changes.

reach.task: Help occasional users complete internal request forms.
reach.learn: Learn common misunderstandings, accessibility needs and reasons requests are returned.

reach.task: Assess the impact of changing fields and report calculations.
reach.learn: Learn schema contracts, dependency tracing and regression checks.

evidence.claim: Structured specifications support deterministic form generation, validation and versioned publication.
A documented report failure involved non-existent AI-generated sources, supporting explicit source checks for drafted content.
User comprehension and tacit downstream dependencies require observation and stakeholder review.

assumptions: The pilot covers a small family of internal forms or reports.
Current versions and approved templates can be identified.
The dependency register starts with known links and is checked by affected users.
Test cases use synthetic or appropriately protected examples.
unknowns: Which forms are documents, system screens or generated reports?
Who has authority to approve each type of change?
Which downstream calculations and unofficial copies depend on existing fields?
Are versioning, approval and publication features already available?
Do changed forms collect employee data or trigger consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which fields cause the most rework without supporting a clear decision?
Can existing forms be retired or merged before rebuilding them?
Which comprehension and accessibility tests should become release checks?
new_work: Maintain field definitions, templates and dependency mappings.
Review drafted wording and investigate unsupported instructions.
Recruit representative users for short tests.
Check that publication retires obsolete versions.
Update validation cases when business definitions change.
tasks.statement: Design, evaluate, recommend, and approve changes of forms and reports.

tasks.short: Plan a study of operational problems, evidence needs and improvement options.

steps.what: Agree the problem, scope and intended decisions with the study sponsor
Collect operating records and existing procedures for the agreed scope
Reconcile records and calculate baseline volumes, delays and costs
Choose hypotheses, study methods, sampling and measures
Write the study plan, evidence requests, milestones and resource needs

loop.input: Study approach, study brief, baseline pack and approved study template.
loop.output: Study plan with source references and explicit evidence gaps.
loop.check: Validate required sections, dates and totals. Analyst checks source support and methodological consistency.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per plan. Unresolved claims remain flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but the rationale must connect situational evidence to the selected methods.

steps.what: Approve the study scope, resources and access conditions

tasks.design: A reusable study workspace on the {WORKFLOW} collects the brief and retrieves permitted evidence from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP} and {DOCS}. Deterministic jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produce a baseline pack for the {BI}; a bounded drafting loop assembles the analyst's chosen approach into a study plan in the {DOCS}. The sponsor approves scope and resources before the study starts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence crossed systems with inconsistent definitions. Templates could structure a plan but could not choose a sound study method.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, metric checks and document generators. Bounded drafting can turn an explicit study approach into readable prose.
tasks.still_hard: Causal inference, representative sampling and agreement on the real problem remain difficult. Missing timestamps and disputed cost allocations can invalidate the baseline.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst frames a testable problem and challenges a sponsor's preferred explanation.

ambition.what: A rapid diagnostic study for small operational teams without dedicated analysis support.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing competing explanations and less time collecting records. A delegated mandate could let them choose diagnostic methods within an approved study budget; budget approval stays with the sponsor.

reach.task: Turn the approved study into a dependency and resource plan.
reach.learn: Critical paths, resource constraints and change control.

reach.task: Design a study of order delays using operational event data.
reach.learn: Queueing, event timestamps and service-level measures.

evidence.claim: Permissioned extracts, deterministic baseline calculations and templated study plans are established technical patterns.
A documented Deloitte report case contained nonexistent citations, supporting source checks on generated study text.
AI used to evaluate workers can fall within the EU AI Act's Annex III employment category.

assumptions: This is a scoped operational study, not an automated individual employment decision.
Record collection includes access requests and export retrieval, so its share exceeds pure screen-reading time.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
GDPR applies to personal data. EU AI Act applicability depends on actual use; consultation follows national rules.
Consent and access estimates cover an ordinary review; formal consultation may take longer.
unknowns: Which operating records are accessible and under what permissions?
Are metric definitions and process identifiers consistent across systems?
Will the study assess individual workers or only operational processes?
Which national consultation rules and internal approval routes apply?
research_questions: Do recorded timestamps measure actual waiting time or only administrative entry time?
Does a structured study template provide enough value without model drafting?
Which proposed causes survive comparison with alternative explanations?
new_work: Resolve data exceptions and maintain metric definitions.
Check draft claims against the evidence pack.
Maintain connectors, templates and access rules.
Review whether new study uses change privacy or consultation requirements.
tasks.statement: Plan study of work problems and procedures, such as organizational change, communications, information flow, integrated production methods, inventory control, or cost analysis.

tasks.short: Assess storage needs, compare equipment and propose a workable layout and purchase recommendation.

steps.what: Survey the available space, current equipment, access routes and storage practices.
Calculate required capacity, growth allowance and equipment dimensions.
Request equipment specifications, prices and delivery information from suitable suppliers.
Compare equipment capacity, dimensions, total cost and delivery constraints.

loop.input: Supplier quotes and specification documents in varying formats.
loop.output: Source-linked dimensions, capacities, price components, delivery terms and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate units and required fields; calculate totals deterministically; verify critical dimensions against source documents.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per quote; missing or conflicting values return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied supplier documents need text extraction. Use direct field mapping instead when structured catalogues are available.

steps.what: Draw alternative equipment layouts in space-planning software.
Walk through options with users and select a practical layout.
Prepare the equipment recommendation, cost summary and installation requirements.
Approve the proposed equipment, layout and expenditure.

tasks.design: A parameterised generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} calculates capacity, compares costs and creates layout options for the {OTHER} space-planning software. Configure quote requests in the {PROCUREMENT}, with a bounded extraction loop for unstructured supplier documents, and generate the recommendation in the {DOCS}. Site measurement, practical layout selection and expenditure approval stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements, catalogue dimensions and local constraints were scattered across drawings and quotes. These infrequent projects rarely justified a custom planning tool.
tasks.enabler_now: Small calculation and drawing generators are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Existing geometry methods can check explicit constraints without needing an autonomous planner.
tasks.still_hard: Measurements, floor loads, escape routes, accessibility and installation feasibility need competent verification. A useful drawing cannot establish site safety or structural suitability.
tasks.human_edge: Notice awkward access, unsafe handling, overlooked building constraints and how staff actually use storage.

ambition.what: Compare reuse, consolidation and purchase before each storage investment

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time redrawing layouts and assembling quote tables, and more time observing use and testing alternatives. They gain no purchase or building-safety approval rights; the facilities manager and budget holder retain those decisions.

reach.task: Plan storage installation around building access and workplace use.
reach.learn: Learn site survey methods, installation sequencing and when specialist checks are needed.

reach.task: Arrange stock locations for practical retrieval and handling.
reach.learn: Learn movement patterns, peak demand and handling constraints that drawings can miss.

evidence.claim: Capacity calculations, quote comparisons and checks against explicit geometric constraints can use deterministic code.
Unstructured supplier documents can be extracted into a common comparison schema with source checks.
Physical suitability and workplace safety require site evidence and competent human review.

assumptions: Storage means physical shelving, cabinets or similar workplace equipment.
The pilot covers one site and a limited equipment catalogue.
A competent person supplies applicable clearances and load constraints.
The generator proposes layouts within supplied constraints; it does not certify compliance.
Build ranges cover the planning aid, not equipment delivery or installation.
unknowns: Are current site drawings accurate and dimensioned?
Which equipment types, floor loads and access restrictions apply?
Can existing space-planning software already generate suitable options?
Are supplier catalogues structured or supplied as documents?
Who must approve installation, safety and expenditure?
Does a workplace change require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can retention changes or consolidation remove the need for new equipment?
Which layout checks can the existing space-planning software already perform?
How often does this task recur, and would configuration cost less than a reusable generator?
new_work: Maintain equipment dimensions, units and cost components.
Verify extracted quote fields and resolve missing specifications.
Update site constraints after building changes.
Check generated layouts against on-site measurements.
Retain specialist reviews and approval evidence with the recommendation.
tasks.statement: Recommend purchase of storage equipment and design area layout to locate equipment in space available.

role_batches.altitude: The management analyst shifts from collecting and assembling material toward causal investigation, experiment design and implementation support. Resource and organizational-change authority stays with existing decision makers unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Computer systems analysis: trace data lineage and define reliable source interfaces.
Project management: turn recommendations into scoped pilots with dependencies and acceptance criteria.
Quality management: distinguish process variation from evidence of improvement.
Business continuity planning: design fallback and rollback arrangements for operational changes.
skills_to_grow: Access design, GDPR awareness and applicable national consultation rules
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a continuous operational improvement service that moves small departmental problems from evidence to a measured pilot, with clear human decisions at resource commitments and organizational changes.

role_batches.altitude: The management analyst spends more time framing studies, observing work and negotiating practical changes. Preparation, evidence assembly and document production become lighter; any new authority to prioritise studies or training must be explicitly delegated.
reach: Project management specialists: turn approved findings into sequenced delivery plans.
Computer systems analysts: translate process needs into testable system requirements.
Quality control systems managers: connect procedure changes to controlled documents and competence evidence.
Logistics analysts: investigate operational delays using event data and field observation.
skills_to_grow: Study design, sampling and causal reasoning.
Change facilitation, privacy assessment and national consultation procedures.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a repeatable operational diagnostic service for teams without dedicated analysts: establish a baseline, observe real work, test competing explanations and take a measurable improvement proposal to the responsible manager.

role_batches.altitude: The management analyst shifts from assembling documents and comparisons toward testing whether procedures work in practice. Delegated authority can cover routine template changes and project readiness checks; legal, expenditure and site-safety decisions remain with designated approvers.
reach: Help administrative services managers introduce records requirements before organisational changes.
Work with computer systems analysts to trace data dependencies and validate form changes.
Help facilities managers compare storage alternatives using verified site constraints.
skills_to_grow: Translate business requirements into testable rules and schemas.
Configure workflows, permissions and version controls.
Trace data lineage and assess change impact.
Evaluate bounded model outputs against approved sources.
Run user observations and practical site reviews.
Understand GDPR and applicable national consultation requirements.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer an internal operational design service that checks records readiness, form usability and physical storage alternatives before teams commit money or introduce new procedures.
